claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 8 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child in hospital/residential accommodation for 15 weeks (>12) and claimant is not regularly spending money on child
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

expected_eligibility.name: Alex
expected_eligibility.reason: Child in hospital/residential accommodation for 15 weeks (>12) and claimant is not regularly spending money on child

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment by getting the first question.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to know about your child or children. 

**How old is your child (or the youngest child if you have more than one)?** 

Please tell me their age. This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply:
- **Under 16 years old** - different rules apply
- **16-19 years old** - different rules apply  
- **20 years old or over** - different rules apply

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex is 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 8 years old, they fall into the **under 16 category**, which means there are automatic qualification pathways available.

Let me move forward with the next set of checks for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check a few things about Alex's work and benefits situation.

**Question 1: Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not in paid work at all?**

Since Alex is 8 years old, I'd expect the answer is that they're not in paid work, but I need to confirm this.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - he's only 8!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! That makes perfect sense - Alex is 8 years old so definitely not working. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 2: Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right?**

Specifically, I'm asking if Alex is receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit

in their own name/in their own right?

For an 8-year-old, the answer is almost certainly no, but I need to confirm this.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 3: Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Since Alex is only 8 years old, I expect the answer is no, but I need to confirm. Apprenticeships are typically for older teenagers and young adults, so this should be straightforward.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in an apprenticeship - he's only 8!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I expected. Let me move on to the next important check - your residency situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency situation. There are several potential pathways that could make you eligible:

**Question 4: Where do you normally live?**

Here are the main options:

1. **Normally live in the UK** - You live in the UK as your main home
2. **Have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** - If you're an EU/EEA citizen
3. **Have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** - With additional conditions (working, seeking work, studying, etc.)
4. **Living abroad as a Crown servant** - Working for the UK government in certain qualifying countries

Which of these applies to your situation? Or if none of these seem to fit, could you tell me more about where you and Alex normally live?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I live in the UK - we're in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's straightforward - you normally live in the UK, which satisfies the residency requirements. Let me move forward to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to confirm your responsibility for Alex. There are a few ways this can be satisfied:

**Question 5: Are you responsible for Alex?**

This means one of the following:
1. **You live with Alex** - Alex lives with you as part of your household
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** - You pay for things like food, clothes, housing, pocket money, or presents (at least equivalent to the Child Benefit amount)
3. **You pay maintenance under a court order or agreement** - Court-ordered or agreed maintenance payments for Alex's care

Which of these applies to your situation with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You live with Alex, which satisfies the responsibility requirement. Let me move forward to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 6: Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or have they claimed in the past?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- A grandparent
- Another family member
- Anyone else

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for each child at any given time.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's clear. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 7: Where is Alex currently living?**

I need to check if any special circumstances apply:
- **In hospital** - Long-term hospital admission
- **In care** - In local authority care or residential care
- **Fostered** - Being fostered by someone else
- **Living normally at home** - With you as their usual home

Which applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex has been in hospital for a while now - a few months actually.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I understand - that's a significant situation. Let me check the specific details about Alex's hospital stay, as there are special rules about how long a child can remain in hospital and still qualify for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to understand the details of Alex's hospital stay better, as there are special rules about time spent in hospital.

**Question 8: How long has Alex been in hospital cumulatively?**

The rules are important here:
- Child Benefit can continue for up to **12 weeks** in hospital
- If Alex has been in hospital for **multiple stays**, I need to add them together IF the gaps between stays were less than 28 days
- If gaps were 28 days or longer, each stay is counted separately

So to clarify:
- Has Alex been in hospital **continuously for a few months** (one ongoing stay)?
- Or has there been **multiple separate admissions** with gaps between them?

And roughly how many weeks total has this been?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been one continuous stay - about 15 weeks now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying. So Alex has been in hospital continuously for about 15 weeks. Let me get the specific constants to verify the exact rules.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see the issue clearly now. According to the rules:

**Hospital Stay Limits:**
- Child Benefit can continue for up to **12 weeks** in hospital
- Alex has been in hospital for **15 weeks continuously**

Since Alex's hospital stay has exceeded the 12-week limit, this affects eligibility. However, let me continue with the next check as the rules also consider whether you're regularly spending on Alex's care while in hospital.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 9: Are you regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital?**

This is important because there's an exception to the 12-week limit. If you're regularly spending money on Alex's care or needs while in hospital (for example: special foods, clothes, entertainment, travel to visit, gifts, etc.), this can help maintain eligibility even beyond the 12 weeks.

Are you regularly spending money on Alex's needs while in hospital?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I haven't been able to afford to spend money on his needs while he's in there.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I understand - that's a difficult situation. Unfortunately, based on the rules, this means Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit is affected. Let me proceed to confirm the outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to deliver this news. Based on the information you've provided, here is the outcome:

---

## **Eligibility Outcome for Alex**

**Result: INELIGIBLE**

**Reason:** Child Benefit stops after 12 weeks in hospital or residential accommodation, unless you are regularly spending money on the child's needs. Since Alex has been in hospital for approximately 15 weeks (exceeding the 12-week limit) and you're not able to regularly spend money on his needs, he does not currently qualify for Child Benefit.

---

## **Important Information:**

**Key Rule:** The 12-week limit applies cumulatively. If there are multiple hospital stays:
- Stays separated by **less than 28 days** count together towards the 12-week limit
- Stays separated by **28 days or more** start the counter fresh

**Possible Exceptions or Next Steps:**

1. **If Alex is discharged soon:** When Alex leaves hospital, you may be able to re-claim Child Benefit from the date he returns home.

2. **If you can start spending regularly on his care:** If your financial situation changes and you're able to spend money on Alex's needs (food, clothes, entertainment, travel to visit, etc.), you might be eligible for an exception. Contact HMRC to discuss this.

3. **Contact HMRC:** Given the complexity of your situation, I'd recommend contacting HMRC directly:
   - **Phone:** 0300 200 3100
   - **Website:** www.gov.uk/child-benefit
   
   They can review your specific circumstances and may be able to discuss any additional support options.

I'm genuinely sorry this is the outcome. I hope Alex recovers well and can return home soon.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I understand. Thank you for explaining that to me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome. I'm glad I could explain the situation clearly, even though it's not the outcome you were hoping for.

To summarise once more:
- Alex's 15-week hospital stay exceeds the 12-week limit for Child Benefit eligibility
- If circumstances change (such as Alex being discharged, or you being able to contribute regularly to his care), you should contact HMRC to reassess your eligibility

**Please don't hesitate to reach out to HMRC if:**
- Alex is discharged from hospital
- Your financial situation improves and you're able to spend on his needs
- You have any other questions or need support

**HMRC Contact Details:**
- **Phone:** 0300 200 3100
- **Website:** www.gov.uk/child-benefit

I wish you and Alex all the best during this difficult time. If you have any other questions or need help with anything else regarding Child Benefit in the future, feel free to ask.

Take care.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I appreciate your help. I'll contact HMRC if things change. Thank you.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome. I'm really glad I could help you understand the situation. 

Best of luck with Alex's recovery, and please do reach out to HMRC when circumstances change - they'll be able to help you get back on track with Child Benefit once Alex is home.

Take care, and wishing you and Alex all the best. 🙏
